course.title: Selenium — Complete Deep Testing Course
course.description: A Selenium-specific, beginner-to-advanced automation course with detailed concepts, practical browser testing, dedicated tasks, debugging, CI integration and a complete learning-platform capstone.
course.curriculumPolicy: Module and lesson counts are determined by the concepts required to learn the testing tool properly; no fixed cross-tool template is imposed.
learningOutcomes: Handle synchronization and test data correctly.
Debug failures and integrate tests into CI.
Build a complete production-style E2E test suite.

modules.title: Selenium Foundations
modules.description: WebDriver, browser automation, sessions and the Selenium ecosystem.

lessons.title: Selenium Foundations
lessons.description: WebDriver, browser automation, sessions and the Selenium ecosystem.
learningObjectives: Apply it to a realistic web-testing workflow.

notes.text: WebDriver, browser automation, sessions and the Selenium ecosystem.

Learn selenium foundations by understanding what the browser automation layer is doing, how the test controls the application, how synchronization works, and how to verify the result without creating fragile tests.

Selenium Foundations is important for building confidence in a real web application. Good automated tests reproduce meaningful user behavior while remaining isolated, deterministic, readable and maintainable.

notes.caption: Add a browser-testing diagram or screenshot-style visual explaining Selenium Foundations.

items: Test behavior and outcomes, not implementation details unnecessarily.
Use stable selectors and deterministic data.

notes.code:
Scenario: Create the first automated browser test.

Automation flow: arrange data -> navigate -> interact -> wait for state -> assert -> capture evidence -> cleanup.

items: Define the user journey or behavior.
Wait for the application state, not an arbitrary delay.
Adding fixed sleeps instead of condition-based waits.
Sharing mutable test data between tests.
Testing implementation details instead of user behavior.
Making one huge E2E test instead of focused journeys.
Use API setup when it makes tests faster and cleaner.
I can explain Selenium Foundations in my own words.
I can automate a small browser workflow.
I can choose a stable locator.
I can synchronize without arbitrary sleeps.
I can diagnose a failing test.

practicals.title: Guided Practical — Selenium Foundations
practicals.objective: Apply Selenium Foundations to a realistic learning-platform test scenario.
steps: Run the test repeatedly to check stability.
Capture debugging evidence if it fails.
practicals.starterCode:
# Selenium — Selenium Foundations
# Scenario: Create the first automated browser test.
practicals.expectedOutput: A stable automated test demonstrating Selenium Foundations.

tasks.title: Dedicated Task — Selenium Foundations
tasks.description: Create the first automated browser test.
requirements: Implement Selenium Foundations using Selenium.
Test a realistic learning-platform flow.
Use stable locators and deterministic state.
Handle relevant failure/edge cases.
Document how to run and debug the test.
acceptanceCriteria: No unnecessary fixed waits are used.
Test data is isolated or safely managed.

quiz.question: What is the main focus of Selenium Foundations?
quiz.answer: Reliable browser/test automation using Selenium
quiz.explanation: The lesson focuses on applying Selenium Foundations to real web testing.

quiz.question: Which is generally better than a fixed sleep in browser automation?
options: Waiting for a meaningful application state
quiz.answer: Waiting for a meaningful application state
quiz.explanation: State-based synchronization is usually faster and more reliable than arbitrary delays.

summary: Learn to maintain and debug the test.
